issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem 1.5 equates the integral of f over S^d with the iterated integral (1/2) \int_{-1}^1 \int_{h^{-1}(s)} f(\omega) d\sigma(\omega) ds. This assumes that the pushforward of the normalized surface measure \sigma on S^d under the coordinate function h(\omega) = \omega_1 is the uniform measure (1/2)ds on [-1, 1], which is true only for d=2. For d >= 3, the pushforward measure has density proportional to (1-s^2)^{(d-2)/2} ds. For example, taking f(\omega) = \omega_1^2 \in P_2(S^d), \int_{S^d} \omega_1^2 d\sigma = 1/(d+1), whereas the iterated integral gives (1/2) \int_{-1}^1 s^2 ds = 1/3 \neq 1/(d+1). Thus, the curve w_{X,M} fails to be a weighted t-design curve on S^d for all d >= 3. (Additionally, the piecewise definition of w_\mathbb{R}(s) in equation (2.1) omits division by \lambda(x_i), leaving w_\mathbb{R} discontinuous across subintervals whenever \lambda(x_i) \neq 1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must construct a piecewise smooth curve on S^d whose parametrization replicates the non-uniform marginal density proportional to (1-s^2)^{(d-2)/2} without derivative blow-up at the poles s = \pm 1, or provide an alternative construction of weighted t-design curves on S^d for d >= 4.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 1.5 fails for all d >= 3. Consequently, the general-dimension existence result in Theorem 1.3 (which relies on Theorem 1.5) is unproven for all d >= 4, and Theorem 1.4 (which also relies on Theorem 1.5) is unproven for all d >= 3.
issues.title: Invalid coordinate projection integration formula for weighted design curves on higher-dimensional spheres
issues.why_classification: Theorem 1.5 is false for all d >= 3, and the main existence claim of Theorem 1.3 for all dimensions d >= 4 as well as Theorem 1.4 for d >= 3 lose their proofs; repairing this requires an essentially new construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This extension to $\varepsilon_t$-approximate $t$-design curves follows exactly as in the original proof, so we appeal to that work \cite[Sections 4-6]{EhlerGrochenig23} to prove Proposition \ref{pro:caps}.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition 5.1 claims that one can construct an approximate t-design curve on S^d from an approximate t-design curve on S^{d-1} by appealing to Sections 4-6 of Ehler and Gröchenig (2023). However, Ehler and Gröchenig only consider d=2 and construct curves on S^2 from scratch by partitioning into 2D spherical caps around points of a spherical design; they prove no inductive dimension-lifting result from S^{d-1} to S^d. Moreover, spherical caps on S^d are d-dimensional regions, so curves living on S^{d-1} cannot directly average polynomials over caps on S^d.

failure_location.quote: Fix $d\in\{2,3,...\}$, $\varepsilon_t\geq0$ for $t\in\Bbb N$, and a sequence $(\alpha_t)_{t=0}^\infty$ of $\varepsilon_t$-approximate $t$-design curves on $S^{d-1}$. There exists a sequence $(\gamma_t)_{t=0}^\infty$ of $\varepsilon_t$-approximate $t$-design curves on $S^d$ of asymptotic order $\ell(\gamma_t)\asymp t^{d-1}\ell(\alpha_t)$ of arc length as $t\to\infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must provide a valid construction and error analysis demonstrating how curves on S^{d-1} can be adapted into approximate t-design curves on S^d, or provide an alternative construction for even-dimensional spheres.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 5.1 is completely unsupported. Because Theorem 1.7 relies solely on Proposition 5.1 and Theorem 1.6, Theorem 1.7 (existence of approximate t-design curves on even-dimensional spheres S^{2n} with length \asymp t^{4n-3}) is left entirely unproven for all n >= 2.
issues.title: Unsubstantiated dimension-lifting proposition for approximate design curves
issues.why_classification: The dependency cited does not exist, leaving the central claim for even-dimensional spheres in Theorem 1.7 entirely without proof for all n >= 2.

issues.failure_explanation: By definition, a hybrid design averages points in its set uniformly with weight \rho/|X|. When replacing a circle component C = S^d \cap P with the vertices X_P of a regular s-gon, the new point set X \cup X_P is given weight \rho' / (|X| + s), where \rho' = \rho + 2\pi/\ell(\gamma). For the linear functional on polynomials vanishing on P to match that of (X, \gamma, \rho), one requires \rho' / (|X| + s) = \rho / |X|, which imposes the rigid constraint s = 2\pi|X| / (\rho \ell(\gamma)). The assertion that this holds for all s > t is false, as choosing different values of s changes the relative weighting between points in X and points in X_P.

failure_location.quote: $(X,\gamma,\rho)$ is a hybrid $t$-design if and only if $(X\cup X_P,\gamma_P,\rho+2\pi/\ell(\gamma))$ is a hybrid $t$-design.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the construction for weighted hybrid designs where X and X_P can carry different weights, or restrict s and the circle radius to the unique values that preserve equal point weights and balance.
issues.overall_effect: Remark 6.2 is false as stated; the biconditional equivalence fails for arbitrary s > t.
issues.title: Invalid weight balancing equivalence in hybrid design characterization
issues.why_classification: The failure can be repaired locally by adjusting the balancing conditions or allowing distinct weights on X and X_P without altering the rest of the paper.
